_meta.indication: JESDUVROQ is indicated for the treatment of anemia due to chronic kidney disease (CKD) in adults who have been receiving dialysis for at least four months.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, open-label (sponsor-blind), active-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter event-driven study; daprodustat vs rhEPO, randomized 1:1.
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects with anemia associated with CKD who are on dialysis who are switched from rhEPO or its analogs.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary: mean change in Hb between baseline and the evaluation period (mean over Weeks 28 to 52), tested for non-inferiority; and time to first occurrence of MACE (composite of all-cause mortality, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke).
pivotal_trials.result: Hb non-inferiority met: adjusted mean treatment difference 0.18 g/dL (95% CI 0.12, 0.24), lower bound above the -0.75 g/dL margin. MACE similar between arms: HR 0.93 (95% CI 0.81, 1.07), upper bound below the prespecified 1.25 risk margin, demonstrating non-inferiority.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=10%) are hypertension, thrombotic vascular events, and abdominal pain. In ASCEND-D, hypertension occurred in 24% (vs 24% rhEPO) and abdominal pain in 11% (vs 8% rhEPO). Adjudicated thrombotic vascular events occurred at 9.8 per 100 PY (vs 11.7 per 100 PY rhEPO).
target_moa: Daprodustat is a hypoxia-inducible factor prolyl hydroxylase (HIF-PH) inhibitor; a reversible inhibitor of HIF-PH1, PH2 and PH3 that stabilizes and increases nuclear accumulation of HIF-1alpha and HIF-2alpha transcription factors, leading to increased transcription of HIF-responsive genes including erythropoietin.
modality: Small molecule (oral inhibitor of HIF-PH enzymes).

boxed_warning.content: Increased risk of death, myocardial infarction, stroke, venous thromboembolism, and thrombosis of vascular access; JESDUVROQ increases the risk of thrombotic vascular events including MACE, and targeting a hemoglobin greater than 11 g/dL is expected to further increase risk.

rems.type: A risk evaluation and mitigation strategy is not necessary to ensure the benefits of daprodustat in the DD population outweigh the risks.

advisory_committee.vote: The Division of Non-Malignant Hematology convened an advisory committee on October 26, 2022. For the dialysis population, the vote was 13 yes vs. 3 no that benefits outweigh risks; for the non-dialysis population the vote was 5 yes vs. 11 no.

summary.text: Daprodustat was submitted by GlaxoSmithKline under the 505(b)(1) pathway as a new molecular entity - the first HIF-PHI in its class - reviewed under standard (not priority) review; NDA 216951 was received 2/1/2022 with a 2/1/2023 PDUFA goal and approved on the first cycle for the dialysis-dependent CKD anemia population (the non-dialysis indication was not approved). An advisory committee was convened on October 26, 2022.

citations.quote: The Applicant, GlaxoSmithKline, Inc., is seeking approval of daprodustat under the 505(b)(1) regulatory pathway, for the treatment of anemia associated with chronic kidney disease in adults on dialysis and not on dialysis. Daprodustat is a new molecular entity, and if approved would be the first marketed drug in the class of hypoxia-inducible factor prolyl-hydroxylase inhibitors (HIF-PHI).
The Division of Non-Malignant Hematology (DNH) convened a virtual advisory committee meeting to discuss daprodustat on October 26, 2022.

requirement.text: 4400-1: Deferred pediatric study under PREA - conduct a trial to evaluate the pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics and safety of Jesduvroq in children and adolescents aged 3 months to under 18 years requiring dialysis (Final Report Submission 02/2030).

citations.quote: 4400-1 Conduct a trial to evaluate the pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics and safety of Jesduvroq for the treatment of anemia associated with chronic kidney disease in children and adolescents aged 3 months to under 18 years requiring dialysis.

requirement.text: 4400-2: Conduct a prospective US observational study (at least 5 years follow-up) to characterize the long-term safety of Jesduvroq in adults with dialysis-dependent CKD versus an ESA comparator, including MACE, thrombotic vascular events, HHF, serious GI bleeds, eye disorders, and hepatic injury.

citations.quote: 4400-2 Conduct a prospective observational study in the United States to characterize the long-term safety (at least 5 years follow up) of Jesduvroq in adults with dialysis-dependent chronic kidney disease treated with the approved dosing regimen of Jesduvroq versus an ESA comparator arm.

requirement.text: 4400-3: Conduct an observational study (at least 5 years follow-up) to assess the risk for malignancy (hematological and non-hematological) in adults with dialysis-dependent CKD treated with Jesduvroq versus an ESA comparator arm.

citations.quote: 4400-3 Conduct an observational study (at least 5 years follow up) to assess the risk for malignancy (hematological and non-hematological) in adults with dialysis-dependent chronic kidney disease with anemia treated with Jesduvroq versus an ESA comparator arm.

requirement.text: 4400-4: Conduct a worldwide descriptive study to collect prospective and retrospective data on women exposed to Jesduvroq during pregnancy to assess pregnancy and maternal complications, and effects on the fetus, neonate and infant.

citations.quote: 4400-4 Conduct a worldwide descriptive study to collect prospective and retrospective data on women exposed to Jesduvroq during pregnancy to assess the risk of pregnancy and maternal complications, adverse effects on the developing fetus and neonate, and adverse effects on the infant.
